# PTF predicate allocation repair, frozen V3

The held V2 zlib build spent most of both sampled intervals in reaching-definition validation. For array initializer calls, rd_sem repeatedly allocated a sorted eligible argument vector and two mapping pairs for every argument during every edge predicate. Newly restored 512-row arrays expose this cost.

V3 adds a borrowed eligible-index iterator and three PTF-only branches. For the eligible nonzero index collection A, used(q) means q belongs to A; defined(q) means q belongs to A or q equals -1 and A is nonempty; flow(s,d) means s belongs to A and d equals s or -1. Actual negative arguments, duplicate indices, missing ARGUMENT_INDEX, FIELD_IDENTIFIER exclusion, and index-zero receiver behavior are preserved. Queried nodes can inherit membership from a valid sibling with the same index. The old mapping constructor remains the specification in the new Rust regression unit; all non-PTF fallbacks and call-return behavior remain unchanged.

Offline exhaustive equivalence covers 8,421 lists and 530,523 predicate checks. All three Rust RD semantics tests pass, including a new 400-case eligibility/index matrix. All 14 full tenth-family outputs are byte-identical to held V2, and the original checker passes all 308 committed blocks using the frozen release producer through a strict recorded Cargo shim. The checker and reference bytes are unchanged.

One separate diagnostic zlib pilot completes in 3.629123 seconds with 488.65625 MiB peak RSS. Its graph and edge files exactly match held V2 hashes. This is one pilot, not repeated acceptance; root owns the unchanged budgets and final resource gates. The unrelated process preflight and full logs are retained. The worker CLI cache constant remains20 because this patch does not touch it; parent integration retains21. No graph behavior, type dimension logic, source locations, array initializers, solver rules, checker, oracle, or budget was altered. Lifetime-drop alternatives remain unimplemented.
